propositions: Three identical O_EXCL file-lock loops exist in enrich_drain, compact_trigger, and gc_trigger, creating code duplication and copy-paste defects.

The drain's release semantics use a single try block that leaks the lock file until the 3600 s ceiling if os.close raises; compact_trigger and gc_trigger use two independent try blocks and must become the shared implementation.
The three implementations differ in stamp bytes (drain appends newline, others do not), logging verbosity, and directory creation patterns, requiring a unified abstraction with parameterization.
Consolidate the lock logic into a new src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py module with stamped_file_lock() and release_stamped_lock() functions, keeping directory creation with callers.
The shared implementation must preserve the drain's reclaim WARNING holder naming via describe_holder callback and warn on stamp write failure across all three workers.
The test monkeypatch.setattr dependencies on compact_trigger._acquire_trigger_lock and release_trigger_lock by name require that both remain module-level attributes.
